A note to you
Two numbers, read with care

Your date of birth carries two numbers that Indian numerology treats as a signature: the Mulank, from your birth day, and the Bhagyank, from the whole date.

Your numbers come from your date of birth alone, with no birth time or place. A Kundli reading is a separate kind of reading.

This report reads them together, not apart, and then looks at your personal years: the one now running and the one ahead. Where a line fits, keep it. Where it does not, leave it.

Everything here follows contemporary numerology writing and is offered for reflection. It is not scientific prediction and not a guarantee of any event.

— Your Axtroshastra analyst

How these are worked out

Mulank is the birth day reduced to a single digit. Bhagyank is every digit of the full date of birth added together, then reduced to a single digit. The numbers 11 and 22 are always taken down to a single digit here, and the working is shown each time.

Contemporary Indian numerology writing reads Mulank as how you go about things and Bhagyank as your direction. Neither is ranked here.

Yours: Mulank 5 (how), Bhagyank 1 (direction).

Core numbers · The pair

Mercury connects, Sun leads

Mulank 5, MercuryContemporary Indian numerology writing links Mulank 5, Mercury, with adaptability, curiosity and communication.
Bhagyank 1, the SunContemporary Indian numerology writing reads Bhagyank 1, the Sun, as a direction toward initiative, self-reliance and taking on leadership over time.
The two togetherRead together, Mulank 5 sets how you go about things and Bhagyank 1 sets where you are headed. In this reading, Mercury's themes (adaptability, curiosity and communication) sit alongside the Sun's themes (initiative, self-reliance and taking on leadership over time).
Planetary links

In the natural-friendship table used in Jyotish, Mercury counts the Sun as a friend, and the Sun counts Mercury as neutral. The table is not mirrored, so both directions are given. This report states the table, not a reading drawn from it.

Numerology is a belief system, not a science. Readings follow contemporary writing, for reflection only.

What carries you, and where to grow

Bars: strength on the left, its growth edge on the right.

A growth lens

These are not flaws. Each growth area is the other face of a strength; left unmanaged, the same trait tips toward restlessness, going it alone and starting more than finishing.

The readAdaptability, direction and fresh starts are your main assets. Keep them as they are, and grow the edge beside each: finish before the next idea, ask earlier, finish before the next start.

Career & Relationships · Work

How you tend to work

Contemporary Indian numerology writing reads Mulank as how you go about work and Bhagyank as the direction your working life takes. The points below are prompts for reflection, not guidance on what to do.

Working style, Mulank 5, Mercury.In work terms, writers describe Mulank 5 as variety, quick exchange of ideas and building connections.
Strengths writers note at work.For Mulank 5: adapting quickly, making connections, resourcefulness. For Bhagyank 1: taking initiative, owning results.
Bringing the two together.Your Mulank 5 may look for variety and room to move. Your Bhagyank 1 may look for a say in the result. Where does your current work already offer each of these, and where does it not?

A point to watch.Writers mention restlessness and inconsistency with Mulank 5. Writers mention difficulty accepting criticism and a pull to take over with Bhagyank 1. These are patterns to notice, not verdicts.
Questions to reflect on.Which task do you leave unfinished when something newer arrives? Which decisions at work do you want to own, and have you said so?
Fields linked with Mulank 5.Contemporary Indian numerology writing links Mulank 5 with business, media and writing. These are interpretations from that writing, not career recommendations. Treat them as questions to explore, not advice.

How this is worked out

Personal year = birth day (14 gives 1 + 4 = 5) + birth month (3) + the digits of the calendar year, reduced to a single digit. Your Personal Year 1 matches your Bhagyank.

Timing

This report counts personal years from 1 January to 31 December. As of 13 November 2026, 49 days remain before your Personal Year 1 begins on 1 January 2027.
